clue.text: Film robot given time to make something noteworthy?

blocks.note: WALL-E is the title robot of the 2008 Pixar film
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A movie robot is given more screen time and becomes something remarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noteworthy' is split cryptically: not remarkable, but worthy of holding notes, i.e. banknotes. The question mark flags the play on the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallet is a pocket case for carrying banknotes, so it is literally a thing fit to hold paper money.

clue.text: Head of finance department supporting gas and electricity provider

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only that letter is kept
in a down entry, a support sits underneath, so these pieces are placed below what they hold up

blocks.note: wind is gas in the digestive sense
the opening letter of the word
an arm is a branch or department of an organisation

explanation.surface: A company's finance director backs a utility that supplies both gas and electricity.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'supporting' means placed below, so the head of finance plus department sits under the gas. 'Gas and electricity provider' reads as one phrase, but 'gas' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind farm is a group of turbines generating power for the grid, so it supplies electric current.

clue.text: Cross and somewhat belligerent

indicators.note: 'somewhat' means only partly, so just a portion of the following word is taken

blocks.note: the letters run inside this word, after its first three

explanation.surface: Someone who is angry and a bit aggressive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like an adjective meaning angry, matching 'belligerent', but it is a noun: a hybrid animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A liger is the hybrid offspring of a male lion and a tigress, so it is a crossbreed between two species.

clue.text: Have tenant periodically

indicators.note: something done periodically happens at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of the word

explanation.walkthrough: 'Have' as in 'have lunch' is the definition; the even letters of the next word supply the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a meal or a snack is to consume food, so the verb works as a common synonym.

clue.text: Mime’s cheek to droop in the auditorium

indicators.note: an auditorium is where an audience listens, so what follows is taken by its sound

blocks.note: lip is insolent talk, cheek
to droop is to sink, which has the same sound as a short form of synchronise

explanation.surface: A mime artist's face sags in the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mime's' reads as possessive but is 'Mime is'. Cheek here is impudence, not a part of the face.
explanation.definitionFit: To lip-synch is to move one's mouth in time with recorded singing without actually performing, which is miming.

clue.text: Announced where the Colossus was? That’s progress!

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so the answer is matched by its sound

blocks.note: the Colossus was a giant statue on the Greek island of Rhodes

explanation.surface: Someone excitedly locates the ancient Colossus and declares a breakthrough.
explanation.walkthrough: The Colossus of Rhodes was one of the Seven Wonders of the ancient world, so its location is spoken as a two-word phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Making inroads means advancing or gaining ground gradually, so the noun stands for headway achieved.

clue.text: For one, Bond Street befouled with eg, can

indicators.note: something befouled is messed up, so these letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: London's smart Bond Street has been dirtied by someone, say, with a tin can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond Street' reads as the London shopping street, but Bond belongs with 'For one' as the definition and only 'Street' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: James Bond is Ian Fleming's fictional spy, so he is one example of a covert operative.

clue.text: Relative accepting jail on organizing risky transaction

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so one piece goes inside the other
organizing means arranging afresh, so these letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: nan is an informal word for grandmother
taken as written

explanation.surface: A family member takes on a dodgy deal while sorting out prison matters.
explanation.walkthrough: The relative opens around the rearranged letters. NINJA stands for 'no income, no job or assets', a borrower of the kind behind the 2008 sub-prime crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: A loan to a borrower with no income, job or assets is a lending deal very likely to default.

clue.text: Solo perhaps conducted after upsetting composer

indicators.note: to upset is to overturn, and in a down clue that flips the word upside down

blocks.note: Han Solo is the Star Wars smuggler, so Han is an example of someone surnamed Solo
to conduct is to lead

explanation.surface: A soloist performs after unsettling the composer of the piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solo perhaps' suggests a musical solo, but the 'perhaps' points to a person named Solo: the Star Wars pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: George Frideric Handel was the Baroque composer of Messiah and Water Music.

clue.text: Condescend to frame small sketch

indicators.note: a frame goes around a picture, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: to deign is to condescend
S is the clothing abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Someone stoops to put a small drawing in a frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frame' and 'sketch' sit naturally together as art words, but frame is the container instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A design is a preliminary drawing or plan showing how something will look, much like an outline drawing.

clue.text: Clothes for undercover agent whir strangely?

indicators.note: something done strangely is done oddly, so these letters come out in an unusual order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A spy's disguise outfit makes a peculiar whirring noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Undercover agent' reads as a spy, but 'undercover' belongs to the definition, meaning under the bedcovers, and 'agent' starts the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightwear is what people put on to sleep beneath the sheets and duvet, a playful sense of being under covers.

clue.text: Official works with Conservative before being unmasked

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
until someone is unmasked they remain anonymous, abbreviated as anon

explanation.surface: A government official teams up with a Tory before being exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Official' looks like the person in the story, but 'Official works' is the definition, as in a writer's authorised output. Anon is short for anonymous.
explanation.definitionFit: An author's canon is the body of writings accepted as genuinely theirs, the authorised list of their output.

clue.text: Get rid of silver held back by one in wedding service?

indicators.note: going back means running the other way, so the letters are read in reverse
something held is gripped inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: to fire someone is to get rid of them from a job
a bride is one of the principals at a wedding
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Someone wants to dispose of the silverware kept by a person at a wedding ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wedding service' looks like a single phrase about a marriage ceremony, but 'service' alone is the definition, an emergency service.
explanation.definitionFit: The fire brigade is one of the emergency services, the organisation that fights fires and rescues people.

clue.text: Eyes up table, possibly being out to improve appearance?

indicators.note: 'possibly' says the letters could form something else, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone eyes up a table, perhaps going out to look smarter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being out' suggests going out on the town; here it means being out cold, asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Beauty sleep is rest said to keep a person looking fresh, so it is unconsciousness taken for the sake of looks.

clue.text: Under stress, uncovered weapon?

indicators.note: uncovering strips away the outside, so the word loses its first and last letters

blocks.note: taxed means strained or under pressure

explanation.surface: Feeling stressed, someone exposes a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for strained is one word; take off its outer letters to leave the weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: An axe is a chopping tool with a heavy blade, used in battle as a weapon since ancient times.

clue.text: Stop whistleblower running into shower, say

blocks.note: a referee blows the whistle in a match
a shower is an example of rain

explanation.surface: Someone hurries into the shower to halt an informer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whistleblower' suggests someone who exposes wrongdoing; here it is the match official with the whistle.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain is to hold back from doing something, so it serves as a verb meaning cease or desist.

clue.text: Part of beach? Definitely sounds like it

indicators.note: the clue says outright that the answer has the same sound as the preceding word

blocks.note: definitely means for sure

explanation.surface: Is this a stretch of beach? Yes, it certainly seems so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Definitely' looks like an answer to the question, but it is the word whose sound gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The foreshore is the strip of shore between high and low tide, a section of the seaside.

clue.text: Closely follow advert in the middle of programme

indicators.note: sitting in the middle of something means being surrounded by it

blocks.note: a show is a TV programme
ad is short for advert

explanation.surface: Viewers watch an advert break in the middle of a TV programme closely.
explanation.walkthrough: Commercial breaks really do come in the middle of programmes, which hides the instruction in plain sight.
explanation.definitionFit: To shadow someone is to tail them secretly, keeping just behind wherever they go.

clue.text: Crystal meth inside stay out!

indicators.note: 'out' can mean wrong or disordered, so these letters are jumbled
to be inside is to be enclosed, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning: keep away while the drug is in the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crystal meth' is a familiar phrase for the drug, but 'Crystal' alone is the definition and 'meth' goes into the shuffled word.
explanation.definitionFit: Amethyst is a purple variety of quartz, a gemstone that forms as a mineral crystal.

clue.text: Free informant captured by US soldiers

indicators.note: someone captured is held inside, so one piece is enclosed by another

blocks.note: GIs are American soldiers
a rat is an informer

explanation.surface: An informer is released after being taken prisoner by American troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' reads as a verb, to release the captive, but it is an adjective meaning costing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratis is Latin-derived and means without charge, so it matches the sense of costing nothing.

clue.text: What may follow tequila — prison

blocks.note: first meaning: a drink of tequila and fizzy mixer, banged on the table and downed
second meaning: slang for jail

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a night of drinking ending behind bars; the two halves are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A tequila slammer is a cocktail named for banging the glass down, and slammer is also slang for jail.

clue.text: Something in chest I’m thinking is on back of ship

blocks.note: the stern is the rear of a vessel
um is the sound of someone pausing to think

explanation.surface: A pirate pondering whether there is treasure in a chest at the rear of the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chest' suggests a sea chest of treasure, but it is the body's chest. 'Is on' puts the thinking noise after the rear of the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The sternum is the breastbone, the flat bone running down the front of the ribcage.

clue.text: Mate’s ship evacuated on northern river

indicators.note: to evacuate is to empty, so the word's insides go and only its outer letters stay

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the word
the Ouse is a river in Yorkshire in the north of England

explanation.surface: A ship's mate abandons a vessel on a river in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mate's' looks like the ship's officer in a possessive, but it is 'Mate is', and mate means partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A spouse is a husband or wife, and mate is an informal word for a life partner.

clue.text: Is fireman climbing on top of French mountains?

indicators.note: climbing goes upward, and in a down clue that runs the letters the other way

blocks.note: taken as written
Fireman Sam is a British children's TV cartoon firefighter
F is the abbreviation for French

explanation.surface: A firefighter scrambling up a range in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French mountains' reads as one phrase, but French gives a single letter. In a down clue 'on top of' places the upward-read part above it.
explanation.definitionFit: A massif is a compact group of mountains forming a single block, such as the Massif Central.

clue.text: Core features of modern car technology

blocks.note: first meaning: the abdominal muscles of the body's core
second meaning: anti-lock braking system

explanation.walkthrough: 'Core features' sounds like key selling points of a car, but core here is the body's midsection.
explanation.definitionFit: Abs is short for abdominal muscles, central to fitness core training, and the initials of the anti-lock braking system in cars.

clue.text: Focus of photograph rather confused

blocks.note: a snap is a casual photograph
out of it means muddled or dazed

explanation.surface: The subject of a picture is a bit blurred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Focus' looks like a camera term to go with photograph, but it is an imperative to someone daydreaming.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Snap out of it!' is an idiom telling a person to stop moping and pay attention, close to saying concentrate.

clue.text: Smoke with one close to Brooklyn Dodger’s boss

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

blocks.note: fag is British slang for a cigarette
I is the Roman numeral for one
the final letter of the borough's name

explanation.surface: The manager of the Brooklyn Dodgers baseball team lights up with someone nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brooklyn Dodger' suggests the old baseball club, but the Dodger is the Artful Dodger of Oliver Twist.
explanation.definitionFit: In Dickens's Oliver Twist, Fagin runs the gang of child pickpockets that includes the Artful Dodger.

clue.text: Mark, get the point!

blocks.note: first meaning: a scratch or notch made on a surface
second meaning: to win a point in a game

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is someone exasperatedly telling Mark to understand; the two parts are separate meanings, a scratch and gaining a point.
explanation.definitionFit: To score is to scratch a line on something, and also to register a goal or point in a contest.

clue.text: Dodge Greek character beginning to get extremely greedy, the muppet!

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, which is all that is kept
the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only those letters are kept

blocks.note: to dodge something is to miss it
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
the opening letter of the word
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone tells a selfish character to stop being so greedy, calling them an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muppet' is British slang for a fool, so the surface reads as an insult; here it is a literal Muppet.
explanation.definitionFit: Miss Piggy is the glamorous pig puppet from The Muppet Show, so she is the Muppet in question.

clue.text: Buddy’s ring cut from stone

indicators.note: cutting something from a whole removes it, so a letter is taken away

blocks.note: an opal is a gemstone
a ring is round, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A friend's ring has been cut out of a gemstone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buddy's' reads as possessive with ring, but it is 'Buddy is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pal is an informal word for a close friend or mate, as is buddy in American usage.

clue.text: Key article about European economic zone

indicators.note: 'about' means around, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: F is a musical key
a report is a newspaper article
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: An important piece of writing concerning the European economic area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key article' reads as a main news story, but key is a musical key and article a piece of journalism. 'European economic zone' sounds like one phrase; European is wordplay only.
explanation.definitionFit: A free port is a designated area where goods may be imported and re-exported without customs duties, a special trade area.

clue.text: Maybe Venus flytrap’s centre put on flat surface

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle, so only the central letter is kept

blocks.note: a plane is a flat surface in geometry
the fourth of seven letters

explanation.surface: The middle of a carnivorous plant is laid on a level surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Venus flytrap' reads as the plant, but Venus belongs to the definition and only the flytrap's middle letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Venus is the second planet from the Sun, so it is one example of a world orbiting a star.
